verses.summary: Those made wretched are in the Fire; sighing and groaning are described.
verses.comparison_note: Different destinies after judgment are a broad motif, but Daniel speaks of resurrection to life or shame, not this description of Fire.

verses.summary: The duration of punishment is expressed with a heavens-and-earth formula and a qualification of divine will.
verses.comparison_note: Avoid treating formulaic duration or divine sovereignty as a traceable external textual relationship without a distinctive passage.

verses.summary: Those made blessed are in the Garden; the verse describes lasting reward with a qualification of divine will.
verses.comparison_note: Eternal life is a possible broad comparison; Daniel does not describe the Qur'anic Garden or the qualifying formulation.

verses.summary: Warning against doubt concerning ancestral worship; previous generations worshipped similarly and receive their full portion.
verses.comparison_note: General critique of inherited worship is not sufficiently distinctive for a source association.

verses.summary: Moses received the Book; disagreements arose about it; adjudication is deferred.
verses.comparison_note: The Torah describes tablets given to Moses, but does not narrate the same later disagreement and delayed judgment in this passage. Original Hebrew and contextual reading pending.

candidates.required_check: Read Hebrew/Aramaic critical text and historical witnesses; evaluate whether shared contrast is too generic.
Check Hebrew original, Septuagint and manuscript dating; do not equate tablets with the Qur'anic entire Book or assert a source for disagreement.

dossier.title: Final destinies and Moses' Scripture: comparative research dossier (unpublished)

sections.chronological_background: The Qur'anic sequence contrasts destinies after judgment (11:106–108), critiques inherited worship (11:109), then invokes Moses receiving scripture and later disagreement (11:110). Earlier Israelite and apocalyptic traditions provide possible comparative contexts, not proven sources.
sections.similarities: Contrasting outcomes and Moses receiving written instruction are potentially shared broad narrative or doctrinal elements.
sections.differences: Daniel's resurrection to life/shame differs from the Qur'anic Fire/Garden and divine-will qualifications; Exodus's tablet scene does not contain 11:110's account of disputes and deferred judgment.
sections.variant_witnesses: Masoretic Hebrew, Greek Daniel traditions and Septuagint/Pentateuch witnesses require collation; none checked here.
sections.dating: Distinguish ancient composition/redaction, extant manuscript dates and later translation dates; no witness dates independently authenticated.
sections.interpretations: Shared religious vocabulary, literary reception, and independent reworking remain possible; direct dependence not established.
